questions.stem: Which of the following is a definition of matter?
choices: Anything that has mass and occupies space
Anything that is transparent
Anything that is hard
Anything that is lustrous
questions.solution: The correct definition of matter is anything that has mass and occupies space, as this is a fundamental scientific property of all matter. The other options describe specific physical characteristics, such as transparency, hardness, or luster, which are not defining features of all matter.

questions.stem: If two glass tumblers have the same capacity, but one is half-filled and the other is fully filled with water, which of the following is true?
choices: The half-filled tumbler has more mass
The fully-filled tumbler has more mass
Both tumblers have the same mass
The mass of the tumblers cannot be determined
questions.solution: The fully-filled tumbler has more mass because it contains more water, and mass is directly related to the amount of substance present. The half-filled tumbler has less water, so it has less mass. Both tumblers cannot have the same mass because they hold different volumes of water, and the mass can be determined by comparing the amounts of water they contain.

questions.stem: If a material is hard, which of the following is most likely to be true about it?
choices: It is easy to bend
It is difficult to compress
It is transparent
It dissolves in water
questions.solution: A hard material is one that resists changes in shape, which means it is difficult to compress. This directly supports the option 'It is difficult to compress.' The other options describe properties like flexibility, transparency, and solubility, which are not related to hardness.

questions.stem: Which of the following materials would be best suited for making a container that allows us to see the contents inside?
choices: Wood
Glass
Plastic
Iron
questions.solution: Glass is the best material for making a container that allows us to see the contents inside because it is transparent, meaning light can pass through it, making objects visible. Wood and iron are opaque, blocking light and preventing visibility. Plastic can be either transparent or opaque, depending on its type, making it less reliable than glass. The correct answer is glass.

questions.stem: A student fills one glass tumbler with 500 mL of water and another with 1 L of water. Which of the following is true?
choices: The mass of the second tumbler is double the first
The volume of the first tumbler is double the second
The density of the second tumbler is higher
The weight of the first tumbler is double the second
questions.solution: Since volume is directly proportional to mass (assuming the same substance and temperature), the mass of the second tumbler, which has twice the volume, will be twice that of the first. Density and weight depend on mass, not just volume, so they are not necessarily double.

questions.stem: If a student uses a balance to measure the mass of a cup filled with sand, and another cup filled with pebbles, and finds that the pebbles are heavier, what can be inferred about the materials?
choices: Pebbles have less volume than sand
Pebbles are less dense than sand
Pebbles occupy more space than sand
Pebbles have more mass than sand
questions.solution: The balance measures mass directly, so if the pebbles are heavier, they must have more mass. Density and volume depend on mass and space occupied, but the experiment only compares mass. The other options make assumptions not supported by the measurement alone.
